scope: Theorem 3.1 (Exact finite-field scalarization) of the manuscript “Nonuniqueness for bounded measurable scalar conductivities in three dimensions” (preprints/Nonuniqueness-for-Bounded-Measurable-Scalar-Conductivities-in-Three-Dimensions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 365 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 35017573c88b681f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 5. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let U ⊂ R3 be a bounded Lipschitz domain. Let A be a measurable symmetric matrix field satisfying c0I ≤ A ≤ C0I almost everywhere in U, 0 < c0 ≤ C0 < ∞. Suppose the real-valued potentials u1, u2 ∈ H1(U) satisfy div(A∇uj) = 0. Assume that there is an open cover of a full-measure subset of U on whose members A, u1, u2 are smooth and have the following local rank property. On each member, a fixed subset of the potentials has everywhere independent gradients, and every remaining potential is a constant affine combination of that subset. The subset may have zero, one, or two elements; a zero-element subset means that both potentials are constant there. There exist constants 0 < a < b < ∞, a measurable scalar a ≤ γ ≤ b, and v1, v2 ∈ H1(U) such that div(γ∇vj) = 0, vj − uj ∈ H1 0 (U), (3.1) Z U γ∇vj · ∇ψ dx = Z U A∇uj · ∇ψ dx for every ψ ∈ H1 (U). (3.2) The bounds a, b may be chosen using only c0, C0.
